committed: Before any implementation output was inspected: this file and the validation contract in ASTROMETRY.md were committed ahead of js/measure/astrometry.js, the oracle fixtures and every measurement. A check that a measurement crosses is a failed check, not a reason to move the bound; only Carl resets a threshold, with a register row.

conventions.pixels: FITS: 1 is the centre of the first pixel, x along a row, y up
conventions.projection: TAN (gnomonic) about the reference sky position, LONPOLE 180, standard coordinates xi (east) and eta (north)
conventions.model: pixel = p0 + P (xi, eta): six parameters (affine) or four (similarity with a stated parity); CRPIX = p0, CD = inverse of P; no distortion terms

orion.what: Five real stars of the bright-star pack (sky/bright-stars.json, J2000.0, positions as the pack rounds them) on a synthetic frame whose pixels come from a truth WCS

field.what: A small field (about 1.4 degrees) of five synthetic stars, for the tangent-point systematic of the default choice

registration.what: Twelve sources moved by a known rotation and shift between two frames, each centroid with its own noise

ensemble.what: Random truth per trial: reference sky position RA uniform 0 to 360 and Dec uniform -60 to 60 degrees, scale log-uniform 0.5 to 60 arcsec per pixel, position angle uniform, parity at random; the affine truth also has an axis ratio within 0.5 percent and a skew within 0.2 degree; 5 to 8 stars uniform over [50, 974] squared at least 100 pixels apart; the stars' own positions with Gaussian noise of the stated sigma on each axis

mismatch.what: The ensemble's matched trials, each with two stars' catalogue entries swapped (their pixels at least 100 apart); the same trials unswapped are the false-alarm count

a1.recoverNoiseless.what: The orion scene without noise and with the tangent point given as the truth's reference position: the largest sky difference over the 21 by 21 grid of pixels

a1.recoverFiveStars.what: The same five stars with noise 0.1 pixel (one fixed seed), tangent point given: the stated one-sigma sky uncertainty at the 21 by 21 grid is within 3.5 sigma of the difference at every grid pixel, and the fit is consistent

a2.defaultTangent.what: The field scene without noise, the tangent point chosen by the rule (mean direction of the stars): the largest position difference over the 21 by 21 grid, in pixels. The model is exact only at the true reference position; the bound is the second-order systematic the roadmap's 'no distortion terms' leaves, with margin over its estimate (half-field squared times the offset, about 0.03 pixel here)

a3.registrationNoiseless.what: Registration of the scene without noise: translation, rotation and every source's mapped position

a3.registrationShift.what: Registration with centroid noise 0.05 pixel on both frames: the largest difference between the recovered and the true mapped position over the twelve sources and the frame centre

a4.projectionVsKernel.what: The projection against the sky kernel's transforms: for a 15 by 15 grid of pixels of the orion truth WCS, the tangent-plane coordinates from the kernel's unit vectors (js/kernels/sky/coords.js unitVector; xi = p.e / p.n, eta = p.n_hat / p.n) against skyOf's, in degrees; and pixelOf of skyOf against the pixel

a4.projectionVsPage.what: skyOf against the page's own reader (js/observatory/wcs.js skyOf) on the same grid, in degrees

b1.oracleProjection.what: Pixel to sky of the synthetic truth WCS on the 21 by 21 grid against astropy.wcs (wcslib), pinned, in degrees

b2.oracleFit.what: The noisy orion fit against astropy.wcs.utils.fit_wcs_from_points (TAN, no SIP) given the same matched stars and the same tangent point: the pixel of each of the 25 sky points of the 5 by 5 grid, from both solutions, largest difference in pixels

b3.oracleRegistration.what: The noisy registration against scipy.linalg.orthogonal_procrustes with a determinant check and the centroid translation, pinned: rotation in radians and translation in pixels

b4.oracleAuthenticHeader.what: The authentic TESS aperture image of the repository (js/data/observations/tessHd209458S56Aperture.js, a TAN header of CDELT and PC) read by fromHeader: pixel to sky on every pixel and on a 20 by 20 pixel extension against astropy.wcs, pinned, in degrees

b5.oracleAuthenticFit.what: A pinned solution of astropy on an authentic frame with matched reference stars
b5.oracleAuthenticFit.status: NOT RUN until Prompt 189 lands an authentic image pack with a catalogue match; nothing was downloaded and nothing fabricated for this leg

c1.coverageAffine.what: The affine ensemble, tangent point given: z = (estimate - truth) / stated sigma for the sky offset (xi and eta, arcsec) at the five test pixels, and for CRPIX x and y, the mean scale and the position angle; fraction with |z| < 1 and with |z| < 1.96

c2.coverageSimilarity.what: The same for the similarity model (a truth that is one), same quantities except skew

c3.coverageCatalogue.what: The affine ensemble with the catalogue's own noise (0.3 arcsec on each sky coordinate, stated)

c4.falseAlarm.what: Fraction of the matched ensemble trials (affine, tangent given) the fit calls inconsistent (p below 0.001)

c5.coverageRegistration.what: Registration ensemble (12 sources, 3000 trials, a random shift, rotation and sources): z of the shift at the five test pixels and of the rotation; one and 1.96 sigma

d1.collinear.what: Three collinear stars (exactly, and with 1e-12 pixel scatter) refuse: status not-constrained, code collinear, no WCS, on 200 random triples

d2.tooFew.what: Zero, one and two stars: not-constrained, code too-few, no WCS

d3.nearCollinear.what: Stars whose smallest-to-largest spread ratio is 0.01 refuse (collinear); 0.05 is accepted

d4.mismatchedCatalogue.what: Two catalogue entries swapped: the fit reports inconsistent (p below 0.001) and says so in its verdict

d5.unsupportedProjections.what: RA---SIN, RA---ARC, RA---ZPN, RA---AIT, RA---CAR, RA---TAN-SIP, RA---TPV, GLON-TAN, a third axis, a missing CD and PC, a singular CD, are each refused by fromHeader with their own code and the name in the message

d6.tooWide.what: Stars more than 60 degrees from the tangent point: not-constrained, code too-wide

d7.malformed.what: A non-finite pixel or sky position, a non-positive sigma, a declination beyond 90 degrees, two stars at one pixel: each refused with a code, never a number

d8.registrationRefusals.what: Fewer than 3 sources: too-few; sources all within one pixel of their centroid: degenerate; a random pairing of two frames' sources (500 trials): inconsistent in at least 99 percent

d9.residualsAlways.what: Every solved result carries one residual per star in pixels and arcseconds, the degrees of freedom and a verdict; a result with no degree of freedom says that no check is possible, and says it is exactly determined

e1.authenticFrame.what: One authentic frame with reference stars solved under a fixed analysis contract
e1.authenticFrame.status: NOT RUN until Prompt 189; no frame fetched, none simulated
